title: Cursors: DECLARE/OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE (slice 4)
description: The dominant pattern in real batch DB2 COBOL (db2-samples: OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE x12, DECLARE cursor x12). Builtin currently raises NotImplementedError. Implement the backend cursor surface end-to-end (declare->open->fetch-loop->close), multi-row, role across statements.
close_reason: Implemented end-to-end in aa32f49: DECLARE/OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE through the backend cursor surface; unit (test_cursor.py) + live DB2 e2e (test_db2_cursor_e2e.py running unmodified cursor.sqb). Required the red-dragon PERFORM-THRU fix (red-dragon-vt3o / 6a283496).

title: EXEC SQL BEGIN/END DECLARE SECTION as no-op
description: Host-var declaration bookends (32 occurrences across db2-samples). The builtin currently would try to execute 'BEGIN DECLARE SECTION' as SQL. Make begin_declare/end_declare no-ops (SQLCODE 0). Needed for every testbed program.
close_reason: No-op CONNECT/DISCONNECT/SET CONNECTION + BEGIN/END DECLARE SECTION with SQLCODE 0

title: EXEC SQL CONNECT / CONNECT RESET as no-op (injected backend)
description: Every db2-samples program issues EXEC SQL CONNECT TO sample / CONNECT ... USER ... USING / CONNECT RESET (80 occurrences). squall uses an injected SqlBackend, so connection directives must be no-ops returning SQLCODE 0 (not executed as SQL). Needed before ANY testbed program runs.
close_reason: No-op CONNECT/DISCONNECT/SET CONNECTION + BEGIN/END DECLARE SECTION with SQLCODE 0

title: Faithful VARCHAR (49-group) codec + consume dclgen JSON for typed validation
description: Build the VARCHAR 49-group read/write codec (len prefix + text), using the dclgen JSON to identify VARCHAR host vars and their LEN/TEXT child fields (the flat data_layout can't express the group structure). Wire binding to consume the JSON: validate the data_layout category agrees with the recorded sql_type (fail loudly on mismatch), and drive typed bind/decode. This is the designed 'generate + consume JSON' slice; the strict coercion seam (squall-ud0 sibling) is where the column-type checks plug in.
close_reason: Core shipped: VARCHAR 49-group dclgen + binding codec (86ee696), dclgen JSON consumed through prepass->strategy->builtin->codec with VARCHAR(9) INSERT/SELECT e2e (a076508). The remaining typed-validation sub-feature is split out to its own issue.

title: dclgen generator: DB schema → host-var copybook + JSON metadata
description: A squall-side DCLGEN: read a SQLite table via PRAGMA table_info and emit (a) a COBOL 01 host-var record copybook and (b) a JSON sidecar of per-field metadata {column, host_var, sql_type, nullable, total_digits, decimal_digits, length}. v1 supports the categories the codec already binds: INTEGER/SMALLINT/BIGINT (binary COMP), DECIMAL/NUMERIC(p,s) (COMP-3), CHAR(n) (PIC X). Raise NotImplementedError (no silent fallback) for VARCHAR/REAL/TEXT-without-length/BLOB. Field naming: column ACCT_ID → ACCT-ID (underscore→hyphen, uppercase), optional prefix. This replaces the hand-written ACCTREC.cpy and is the foundation for the CRUD capstone.
close_reason: Generator built + verified against real ProLeap data_layout; 14 tests

title: Full-pipeline CRUD capstone integration test (dclgen → COPY → ProLeap → lower → link → CRUD)
description: One integration test driving the whole vertical on a GENERATED copybook: run dclgen on a seeded SQLite table → write copybook+JSON → a COBOL program that EXEC SQL INCLUDEs the generated record → apply_sql_prepass rewrites INCLUDE→COPY → ProLeap inlines it → lower → compile → link → run on the real VMState, performing INSERT, SELECT (verify), UPDATE, SELECT (verify), DELETE (verify) with SQLCODE checks throughout. The builtin already handles DML; this is the first e2e exercising INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE through the real pipeline. v1 table uses INTEGER/DECIMAL/CHAR columns (VARCHAR deferred).
close_reason: CRUD capstone passing end-to-end on a dclgen-generated copybook

title: Richer SQL model types: eliminate None via null-object sums + proper enums
description: ParsedSql is a flat dataclass of X|None Optionals where the strings are actually tiny closed sets. Refactor to a single ParsedSql whose every field is a non-optional value of a small sum type with an explicit null object (no None anywhere): Kind/WheneverCondition as proper enum.Enum (NOT StrEnum — no implicit str comparability); WheneverAction/CursorRef/IncludeRef/ConnectSpec/DbName as frozen-dataclass unions with empty-dataclass null objects. Types are PURE DATA (no interpreter imports); emit/resolve behavior stays in strategy/binding via match. Parameterize loose collections: _plans: list[ParsedSql], cursors: dict[str, ParsedSql], field_meta: Mapping[str, FieldMeta] (TypedDict). Pure type refactor, zero behaviour change; 267 existing tests are the net. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-15-sql-model-rich-types-design.md
close_reason: ParsedSql fully typed: Kind/WheneverCondition proper enums (no implicit str ==); CursorRef/IncludeRef/ConnectSpec/DbName/WheneverAction frozen-dataclass sums with explicit null objects — no None in the model. Collections parameterized (list[ParsedSql], dict[str, ParsedSql], Mapping[str, FieldMeta] TypedDict). Pure-data model in squall/parser/sql_model.py; emit/resolve behaviour stays in strategy/binding via match. Zero behaviour change; 271 tests green. pyright noise from tuple[str|None,...]/unparameterized collections removed; remaining pyright items are pre-existing lark Token/Tree narrowing + the build_query scanner.

title: __sql_session_end builtin: close all cursors + SYNCPOINT (reset SQL session)
description: Expose a named builtin (e.g. __sql_session_end) that closes all open cursors and SYNCPOINTs the unit of work (commit on normal end, rollback on abend). This is the squall-side hook cicada calls at a pseudo-conversational RETURN to reset the SQL session per turn — modelling real CICS task-end (implicit SYNCPOINT + cursor close at thread dealloc, incl. WITH HOLD). Standalone squall never calls it; it exists for the cicada+DB2 compose. Small: reuse the cursor-registry close + the COMMIT/ROLLBACK already built (618ddf5). Composition is name-convention only (no cics<->squall import).

title: Typed validation: data_layout category must agree with dclgen sql_type (fail loud)
description: Split out of squall-6kp (codec + JSON consumption shipped in a076508). When binding a host var that carries dclgen field_meta, validate that ProLeap's data_layout category agrees with the recorded dclgen category/sql_type, and fail LOUD on mismatch — catching copybook/schema drift (e.g. dclgen generated BINARY but the inlined copybook parsed as something else, or a VARCHAR group is missing its -LEN/-TEXT children). For VARCHAR: assert the len_var child is BINARY and the text_var child is ALPHANUMERIC. For scalar kinds: assert data_layout[host_var].category == dclgen category. Runs where data_layout is available (bind time / first builtin run). TDD: a deliberately-mismatched sidecar must raise. No existing fields mismatch, so it is additive.
close_reason: validate_field_meta fails loud (FieldMetaMismatch) on dclgen/data_layout category drift: scalars by category equality, VARCHAR by its 49-group children (len_var BINARY, text_var ALPHANUMERIC); a host var missing from data_layout raises via _require_field. Run once on the first __exec_sql call (nonlocal guard; earliest data_layout is populated). Additive — the COMP-3/VARCHAR e2e exercise it on real ProLeap data_layout and pass (vocabularies agree); empty field_meta is a no-op. 278 tests green.

title: WHENEVER SQLERROR / SQLWARN: program-controlled error branching
description: Surfaced reviewing Db2Backend error handling. Today a SQL failure sets a (now real) negative SQLCODE and execution continues — faithful to the DEFAULT 'WHENEVER SQLERROR CONTINUE'. But real embedded SQL lets a program declare 'EXEC SQL WHENEVER SQLERROR GOTO handler' / 'PERFORM' / 'STOP', and the precompiler then auto-inserts a SQLCODE check+branch after every EXEC SQL statement. Implement WHENEVER (SQLERROR/SQLWARN/NOT FOUND -> CONTINUE/GOTO/PERFORM) so a program can opt into automatic error branching/halting instead of hand-checking SQLCODE. This is the 'should it halt on errors' mechanism: the backend stays faithful (SQLCODE + continue); WHENEVER is where halting/branching is expressed, program-controlled. Faithful numeric SQLCODE (get_sqlcode) already landed (bbfd4f7).
close_reason: Slice 1 shipped: WHENEVER SQLERROR (<0) / NOT FOUND (=100) with CONTINUE / GO TO. Implemented as a real precompiler directive — strategy keeps lexically-scoped per-condition state and lowers a synthetic IF SQLCODE <cmp> <val> GO TO target via ctx.lower_statement after each non-whenever statement (reuses RedDragon IF+GOTO lowering; no raw-IR branch, no label-naming coupling). Removed the latent bug where WHENEVER lowered to a __exec_sql query. 267 tests green incl. DB2 e2e (WHENEVER SQLERROR GO TO branches to handler). SQLWARNING deferred (needs SQLWARN population / squall-ud0); PERFORM/STOP are not DB2 WHENEVER actions. Found+filed a ProLeap EXEC SQL preprocessor bug in red-dragon (underscore/literal patterns -> 'missing END_EXEC').

title: Endianness-aware binary codec (COMP big-endian vs COMP-5 native)
description: squall's SQLCA is standardized on COMP (big-endian) and squall's _binary codec is big-endian — self-consistent in the closed squall+RedDragon system (no real Db2 wire to match), which is why the static.sqb SQLCA (SQLCODE=0) round-trips fine. But db2-samples DATA host vars are often COMP-5 (native/little-endian). If RedDragon decodes COMP-5 as little-endian while squall's codec is big-endian, a COMP-5 numeric host var would mismatch. Verify RedDragon's COMP-5 handling and, if it differs from COMP, make _binary_decode/_binary_encode honor the field's endianness (COMP vs COMP-5) per data_layout. Trigger: the first testbed program that binds a non-zero COMP-5 numeric host var.
close_reason: Investigated for criticality: COMP-5 endianness is a NON-issue. squall's binary codec round-trips COMP-5 self-consistently (big-endian), and RedDragon maps COMP-5 -> BINARY -> big-endian too, so values are correct. The observed cursor.sqb symptom (dept not displaying) was NOT COMP-5: it was a RedDragon multi-operand DISPLAY bug (only the first operand emitted) — filed + fixed as red-dragon-8g6r (e6fe21c7), bumped here in ddd30c8. cursor.sqb now displays 'SANDERS  in dept. 20 is a manager' etc. No squall-side change needed for COMP-5.

title: Faithful CONNECT: backend registry + connection lifecycle (not a no-op)
description:
CONNECT/DISCONNECT/SET CONNECTION/CONNECT RESET are currently no-ops (SQLCODE 0) because squall is handed a single pre-established SqlBackend. This discards real semantics:
- Database-name routing: CONNECT TO <name> selects WHICH database; multiple CONNECT targets collapse onto one backend today.
- Connection lifecycle: after CONNECT RESET, the next SQL should fail with SQLCODE -1024 (no connection); squall keeps working.
- Auth: USER/USING credentials are ignored.

Faithful model: squall holds a {database-name -> SqlBackend} registry. CONNECT TO <name> looks up + sets the ACTIVE backend; SET CONNECTION switches; CONNECT RESET clears; SQL before any connect / after reset returns -1024. The single-backend case becomes a one-entry registry with an implicit connect. Fine to defer while the testbed is single-database (CONNECT TO sample), but needed for multi-DB / lifecycle fidelity.
close_reason: Faithful CONNECT shipped: name->backend registry, per-run connection lifecycle (always-disconnected start; -1024 no-connection / -1013 unknown-db / -1338 not-established), idempotent re-connect with ignored USER/USING creds (testbed double-CONNECT idiom), CONNECT TO / SET CONNECTION / DISCONNECT / CONNECT RESET. Structured CONNECT grammar (no catch-all value-matching). 261 tests green incl. two-real-DB2-database routing e2e (MOJO+MOJO2). Out of scope (not regressions): credential validation, two-phase commit, cicada pseudo-conversational reset (cicada-6hv/squall-ipq).

title: COMMIT / ROLLBACK (slice 5)
description: Transaction control (db2-samples: COMMIT x7, ROLLBACK x6). Map to the SqliteBackend's transaction state.
close_reason: Shipped in 618ddf5: COMMIT/ROLLBACK dispatch + commit()/rollback() on the backend protocol; SQLite/Db2 autocommit disabled for explicit transactions; e2e drives the real db2-samples updat.sqb (UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT then ROLLBACK) against live DB2.

title: Db2 SAMPLE schema in SQLite for the testbed
description: db2-samples programs target the Db2 SAMPLE database (EMPLOYEE, STAFF, DEPARTMENT, ...). Recreate the needed tables + seed data in SQLite so the programs run standalone under squall. Schema is IBM-documented.

title: Tolerant host-var/column type coercion (convert + SQLWARN + indicator)
description:
The coercion layer currently fails strict: any host-var (PIC-derived) type vs column (metadata) type mismatch aborts the statement with a genuine-failure SQLCODE (-301), writing nothing. This issue tracks making it tolerant, matching production DB2 SQL assignment rules:

- Bucket 1 (convertible, lossless): silently convert across compatible types (numeric<->numeric, DATE<->CHAR, narrowing into wider fields). SQLCODE 0.
- Bucket 2 (convertible, lossy): convert WITH a diagnostic. String truncation -> keep SQLCODE 0, set SQLWARN1='W', and if an indicator variable is supplied set it to the ORIGINAL (pre-truncation) length. Numeric fractional truncation behaves analogously.
- Bucket 3 (won't fit / incompatible): the genuine failures the strict layer already returns, refined to the right codes — -304 (value out of range for host var on fetch), -302 (input host var out of range for column), -301 (incompatible data type).

Depends on: the NULL-indicator host-var plumbing (:VAR:IND) being threaded through binding, since bucket-2 truncation reporting uses the indicator. The strict coercion seam built now is the branch point this fills in.
